'ALL TWELVE SHARE ONE SCALE' IS FALSE. k = min((cw-24)/w,(chh-24)/h)*0.96 is a per-image contain fit; each asset gets its own k. Measured source aspects in the named pools run 0.42 (iphone-15-pro-back-gold) to 1.64 (ip-angle-back-topdown) — a 4x spread. A 0.42 portrait renders ~139x323 and a 1.64 landscape renders ~211x129 in the same cell. Adjacent phones will differ in apparent size by more than 2x. Also 'no free-floating extras' and 'no overlap' are guaranteed by the cell fit, but 'no phone is bigger than its neighbour' is not.

problems: The theme's entire identity is 'Pool is exactly 4, which with 4 columns makes index=(n+seed)%4 repeat one unit per column in all three rows: deliberate vertical colour stripes.' The engine sets pool.length itself (slice(0,12) of 55 candidates), so pool.length is always 12 and the columns never form. 'Fix the order left to right — black, blue, gold, white — so the stripe reads as a colour chart' requires an author-set order. The engine iterates pool in the order it derived it and offsets by seed; there is no field for a fixed order, and (n+sd)%4 rotates the columns by seed anyway, so even with a 4-unit pool the left-to-right order changes card to card.
One of the four colourways is a macro crop: iphone-15-pro-back-black (1841x1663) is a cropped camera bump, so the 'colour chart' would show three phones and one dark blob.

The four aspects are 1.11, 0.43, 0.42 and 0.88. Contain-fitted to identical cells, the blue and gold columns render ~139x323 and the black column ~211x190 — the chart reads as four different-sized objects, not four finishes of one product.
cd06 measured 35%; cd04 measured 55%. The weaker palette leads.
Russo One is in STYLE.tech and STYLE.bold; the FACE STYLE data puts bold at 33% and tech at 50%, against stencil 60% and grotesque 56%. It is the weakest display choice in the collection.

problems: FATAL — THE ENGINE CAN NEVER GIVE THIS THEME ITS mustShow, AND WILL ALWAYS GIVE IT ITS neverShow. retheme_lab.mjs:2773 computes `const ok = pool.filter(f => !BLANK.test(f))` before choosing the hero at 2777. BLANK (line 45) explicitly names strip-boxes, strip-boxes-fan, strip-boxes-pile-large, strip-box-single, strip-boxes-row-five, strip-boxes-stack, strip-boxes-cash and strip-vials-pile. For strips that leaves ok = ['strip-kit-meter'] and nothing else. So every card renders strip-kit-meter — which this theme's own neverShow bans by name — and never renders strip-boxes, which its mustShow requires. Every single card violates its own rules.

FATAL — THE mustShow ASSET IS NOT WHAT THE THEME SAYS IT IS. I converted strip-boxes.webp and blew it up 3x. It is not 'a fan of loose test strips with gold contact bars'. Every object in the fan is a two-ended chimera: one end has the black-and-gold electrode contacts of a glucose strip, the other end is a wide white body carrying a rectangular RESULT WINDOW and a small display bezel — the head of a digital lateral-flow / home-test stick. There is also a ghosted semi-transparent smear through the centre-right of the fan, which is the 'faint overlapping product pile' the owner switched OFF. The collectionNote's Fact #2 correctly convicted strip-boxes-fan and strip-boxes-pile-large (I confirmed both: blank white boxes plus a C/T/S/ID: cassette showing a positive line, and plain kraft cubes) but then cleared this file, which is the same defect.
THE PROJECT ALREADY AGREES. BLANK's comment reads 'strips: diabetes only' and the list names strip-boxes. The codebase had already classified this asset as unusable; the collection re-approved it.
RESOLUTION IS TOO LOW FOR ITS OWN SPEC. strip-boxes.webp is 444x418. Drawn at 0.62W of a 1080 card (~670px) it is a 1.5x upscale of an already soft, artifact-ridden image.
fixes: Delete this theme. There is no approved strips cutout it can be rebuilt on: all four (strip-boxes, strip-boxes-fan, strip-boxes-pile-large, strip-kit-meter) fail on inspection, and three of the four are already in BLANK.

problems: The paper spec is exactly right — retheme_lab.mjs:615 defines paper:grid as paper #f7f9fb, grid #b9cbe2, gap 48, and 2627 sets scrim 0.001. Both match the theme verbatim. So do the HIGHLIGHT and STICKY arrays at 2601-2602. This is the best-verified groundSpec in the collection.

THE SHEET CANNOT BE PINNED, AND THE DEFAULT IS THE BANNED ONE. Line 2619 is `const sheet = ['paper:ruled','paper:legal','paper:grid','paper:dots','paper:ruled'][seed % 5]`. It is seed-driven with no override. paper:grid comes up 1 time in 5; paper:ruled — which this theme's neverShow forbids, and which is clinic-chart-ruled's whole identity — comes up 2 times in 5. Four cards in five show the wrong sheet, and two in five collide with another theme in the collection.

RADIANS/DEGREES ERROR. groundSpec says 'the hand-set tilt stays at ±0.8 rad on the highlighter and ±1.2 on the sticky'. retheme_lab.mjs:1439 reads `Math.abs((l.props.angle || 0) * Math.PI / 180)` — props.angle is DEGREES. The real defaults are 0.8° and 1.2°, an almost invisible tilt, not the 46° and 69° the theme describes. The 'no more' constraint is describing a scatter that does not exist.

THE HIGHLIGHTER AND STICKY COLOURS CANNOT BE PINNED EITHER. Lines 2642 and 2644 select by `seed % HIGHLIGHT.length` and `(seed+1) % STICKY.length`. 'Pin both to the cool entries' needs a code change the collection did not list among its two.

THE lp05 AND lp01 SUPPORTS ARE THE COLOURS THE COLLECTION BANNED. lp05 support is #de6116 (orange), lp01 support is #9d8518 (mustard). The collectionNote says the collection carries 'never magenta, violet, mustard or brown'. clinic-chart-ruled correctly bans its own lp09 coral and lp03 pink as fills; this theme bans neither of its two.
Carries the fake 'Sinatore' meter (see clinic-counter-white), but small — at 0.34W the bezel wordmark renders ~48px wide and is not legible.

problems: FALSE ENGINE FACT #1 (invalidates 6 of 10 imagery sections). The note says 'the wall pool is the deck's own cuts prefixes sliced to 12, so it can never mix categories'. retheme_lab.mjs:2893-2899 builds the wall as fromDeck UNION fromSubject: `cand = [...new Set(fromDeck.concat(fromSubject))]` where fromSubject = every ALLCUTS entry matching SUBJECTS[subject].cut. So a sub-deck NEVER narrows the wall — the bullion sub-deck's wall is the whole silver shelf, and the coins wall always contains gold-coins-pile, silver-coins-spill and silver-coins-tube.

FALSE ENGINE FACT #2 (unmentioned). Two filters the note never names remove named cells: `MULTI = /-(pair|trio|group|set|lineup|quad|six|nine|five|three|fan)\b|...|-row\b/i` (line 2892) and `width >= 240` (line 2900). MULTI deletes gold-bars-fan, gold-bars-row, gold-bracelet-pair, silver-bars-row, silver-flatware-set, coin-graded-fan-three, coin-silver-dollar-pair from every wall. Width deletes coin-slab (144) and coin-single-large (223) from every wall automatically.

'ground: tile'/'cast' is only honoured through the LOOKS mechanism (line 2853-2854, `lookGround`). assets/looks.json is an empty placeholder (`"looks": []`), and a look record's key field is `key`, not `id` (line 2733: `LOOKS.find(L => L.key === e.look)`). As written these ten records cannot load.

A look does NOT own its category. The card's cat comes from `RING[(base+e.v)%8]` (line 2698) — phones, gold, cars, pokemon, coins, silver, sports, strips. `categories: ["gold"]` is read by nothing. LAB_CATS only filters donor templates (line 2695); when the ring asks for a category the filtered list cannot supply, line 2701 borrows a template and overrides its cat. So each theme gets its own category on about 1 card in 8.

`variations` is a COUNT, not a spec (line 553-560: `vars = (L.variations||[]).length`, then `pal = L.palettes[v % palettes.length]`). Only the palette and the seed change. Every variation that describes a compositional change — 'no hero cutout', 'four review cards instead of three', 'GOLD BUYER stencilled in the top gutter', 'the copy stack moving right' — is unimplementable from a look record.

Mark colour is hardcoded per category and defeats family rule 1 on 7 of the 10 themes. ELEMENTS.gold.colors = ['#f2c14e','#c9950f','#fff1b8'] and ELEMENTS.coins.colors = ['#f2c14e','#d9d9d9','#c9950f'] (lines 2353-2355); addElements uses `E.colors || [th.accent, ...]` (line 2535). Every drawn mark on a gold or coins card is painted amber-gold. No neverShow addresses mark colour.

'no photograph, no scene, no cash pile, no abstract gradient, no slab frame anywhere' is true but three of those are already impossible, so the entries are noise: slabFrame returns early unless cat is pokemon|sports (line 2372 `if (!/pokemon|sports/.test(cat)) return;`), and with a look ground pinned the cash and abstract grounds are overwritten by the tile/cast branch before export.

THE NORMALISATION THE THEME FORBIDS IS EXACTLY WHAT THE ENGINE DOES, and I computed the result.
